decisions.reason: Product A has been on a dedicated page for two years, indicating substantial sunk costs and public commitment that drive escalation of commitment.
Like Product A, Product B has two years of dedicated web presence, so management persists to justify earlier investment.
Product C has its own page, showing visible commitment, and early results are likely attributed to temporary causes, favoring persistence.
Product D's dedicated page reflects public commitment, and escalation logic makes management reluctant to drop it after one year.
Product E is similarly committed via its own page, so sunk costs and justification pressures lead to keeping it.
Product F is only mentioned on the website, indicating less public commitment, but the firm's investment still leads to persistence, albeit with higher drop probability.
